title: Cyrus and the Protocol
premise: Dominic Halloran, navigator of the freighter Cyrus, discovers that the ship's hold contains illegal memory backups of the colonists of Meridian Station—a colony officially declared lost and legally erased. When the colony's surviving children begin sharing a collective dream broadcast from a failing relay at the edge of dead space, Dominic realizes the backups are not cargo but witnesses: the only complete record of a corporate massacre the Consortium buried. Racing a decaying signal and a Consortium salvage fleet, she must reach the relay, wake the backups as legal testimony, and choose between her own survival and broadcasting the truth. In the end, the children's dream becomes the testimony that convicts the Consortium, and Dominic—her own backup now among them—becomes the bridge between the dead colony and its orphaned heirs.
about_author: Astrid Blackwood is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade listening to signals no one else claimed. She writes science fiction about people who keep records when institutions prefer forgetting.

chapters.title: The Hold Below
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. During a routine inspection of the Cyrus's sealed hold, Dominic finds crates labeled MERIDIAN-7 and a manifest listing 412 'biological archives'—memory backups of people listed as never having existed. Emotional beat: quiet dread; the first crack in her ordered life.

chapters.title: Manifest of Ghosts
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. She cross-references the backups against public records and finds Meridian Station scrubbed from every database, its survivors reclassified as statistical error. The captain warns her to stop asking. Beat: isolation—the loneliness of knowing something everyone is paid to forget.

chapters.title: Children Who Dream Together
chapters.summary: POV Idris, a twelve-year-old on the waystation Thessaly, one of several children suddenly sharing an identical dream: a red field, a voice counting down, a woman saying 'remember us.' Their parents call it a fad. Beat: uncanny wonder turning to fear.

chapters.title: Signal in Dead Space
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. The Cyrus diverts near the coordinates in the dream and detects a faint repeating transmission from a relay at the edge of dead space—the same countdown. She realizes the backups are resonating with it. Beat: awe and vertigo.

chapters.title: What the Backups Remember
chapters.summary: POV Dominic, risking court-martial, interfaces with one backup: Elena Vashti, Meridian's chief engineer, who recounts the station's final days—Concorde Mining sealing the airlocks over a labor dispute gone lethal. Beat: grief; history made flesh.

chapters.title: The Consortium's Clean Hands
chapters.summary: POV Serrano, a Consortium compliance officer, tasked with locating and destroying 'unregistered archival material.' He is efficient, loyal, and beginning to read the files he burns. Beat: cold procedure shadowed by doubt.

chapters.title: Thessaly Interlude
chapters.summary: POV Idris. The dreaming children begin drawing the same woman—Elena—and reciting names they've never heard. A teacher contacts an off-world journalist; the message is intercepted. Beat: innocence colliding with surveillance.

chapters.title: Orders to Burn
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. The Cyrus receives new orders: deliver the hold's contents to a Consortium reclaim vessel for 'sanitization.' The captain, complicit for years, finally confesses he was paid to carry the backups nowhere forever. Beat: betrayal and reluctant alliance.

chapters.title: Running Dark
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. She cuts the Cyrus's transponder and takes the ship off-grid toward the relay, with the captain locked in his cabin and two sympathetic crew aboard. Beat: point of no return; terror and exhilaration.

chapters.title: Serrano Gives Chase
chapters.summary: POV Serrano. The salvage fleet pursues; Serrano reads Elena Vashti's file during the burn and learns his own father died at Meridian, erased like the rest. Beat: the hunter cracking open.

chapters.title: The Dream Widens
chapters.summary: POV Idris. Children on three more stations join the dream; the countdown in it accelerates. Idris realizes the dream isn't haunting them—it's asking for help reaching the relay. Beat: agency discovered in the young.

chapters.title: Dead Space Navigation
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. Navigating uncharted space without beacons, guided by fragments of Elena's memories of the original route, Dominic nearly loses the ship to a debris shoal. Beat: endurance; trust in the dead as pilots.

chapters.title: Mutiny of the Small
chapters.summary: POV Idris. The dreaming children coordinate through their shared dream and sabotage a Consortium tracking array on Thessaly, buying the Cyrus time. First consequences: one child is detained. Beat: courage with a cost.

chapters.title: The Relay at the Edge
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. The Cyrus reaches the relay—a jury-rigged monument built by Meridian's last survivors, still transmitting their testimony into a void no one listens to. Beat: reverence; arriving at a grave that is also a lighthouse.

chapters.title: Elena's Last Log
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. The full record: the massacre, the cover-up, and the survivors' plan to seed their memories into every backup and broadcast until someone remembered. The countdown is the relay's failing power. Beat: sorrow transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: Interception
chapters.summary: POV Serrano. The salvage fleet arrives. Serrano, ordered to destroy the relay, instead transmits the evidence to an independent tribunal before his own officers arrest him. Beat: defection; justice chosen over obedience.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. Under fire, she links the 412 backups to the relay and pushes the full testimony onto every open channel in settled space. The ship takes critical damage; the captain dies buying her minutes. Beat: climax—sacrifice as testimony.

chapters.title: The Dream Fulfilled
chapters.summary: POV Idris. Across the stations, the dream ends—not with the countdown but with 412 voices saying thank you. The detained child is released as the news breaks. Beat: catharsis; mourning braided with relief.

chapters.title: Tribunal of the Remembered
chapters.summary: POV Serrano, testifying. The backups are ruled admissible as posthumous testimony; Concorde's directors face charges. It is imperfect, partial justice—but it is outside nothing now; it is law catching up to truth. Beat: hard-won vindication.

chapters.title: Heirs of Meridian
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. The orphaned children of the diaspora are formally recognized as Meridian's heirs; the relay becomes a memorial. Dominic, injured and stripped of rank, is offered amnesty and refuses the silence that comes with it. Beat: reckoning with what truth costs.

chapters.title: Backups Sleeping No More
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. At the rebuilt relay, the backups are given the choice to remain archived or be rendered into public record and memorial simulation. Elena chooses to speak, once, to the children. Beat: tenderness; the dead given voice by consent, not extraction.

chapters.title: Cyrus, Underway
chapters.summary: POV Dominic, closing frame. She signs on to a small ship crewed partly by Meridian's grown children, carrying testimony—not cargo—to places that have forgotten something too. The last line mirrors the first inspection log: hold empty, conscience full. Beat: resolution; inheritance carried forward.
